child = system.file("rmarkdown", "shared", "glossary.Rmd", package = "HowMaHiCo").
(Do not paste that as a fenced r-chunk example in this comment: knitr parses
chunk headers even inside HTML comments, so an example fence would re-include
this file and duplicate its chunk labels.)

It explains the counting units, then renders pep_all_glossary() as a table, so

every skeleton derives from MHCclass via mhc_length_window() in its setup chunk.
-->

## What is counted

* **Peptides** (e.g. in the barplots) include distinct peptidoforms, so one
  sequence carrying two different modifications counts twice -- although most
  peptides are detected in a single peptidoform.
* **Sequences** (e.g. in the Venn and UpSet plots) are stripped sequences,
  counted once regardless of their modifications.
* **Parent proteins** are the proteins the peptides were assigned to. For DIA-NN
  and PEAKS the accession is a protein *group*, so this is a count of groups.
* **Selected peptides / sequences** are those whose length falls inside the
  expected ligand window for this run,
  `r paste0(shortpep_range[1], " to ", shortpep_range[2], " amino acids")`
  (set by `MHCclass`, or by `ShortPeptideLengthMin`/`Max` for a custom window).
  Everything else is reported as "others".

## Columns of the results table

The long-format table behind every section of this report (`pep_all`, exported
as `pep_all.csv`) carries one row per peptide-sample observation:

```{r glossary-pep-all-table, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
pep_all_glossary() |>
  kable(format = "html", caption = "pep_all columns") |>
  kable_paper("hover", full_width = FALSE) |>
  kableExtra::column_spec(1, bold = TRUE)
```

```{r glossary-pepchem, echo=FALSE, results='asis', message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Only the peptide-chemistry report sets glossary_pepchem <- TRUE; every other
# report skips this table (and its heading) entirely.
if (isTRUE(get0("glossary_pepchem", inherits = TRUE))) {
  glossary_ph <- if (!is.null(params$ChargePh)) params$ChargePh else 7.4
  cat("\n\n## Physicochemical descriptors\n\n",
      "The per-peptide descriptors of this report, computed once per unique ",
      "sequence by `peptide_properties()`:\n\n", sep = "")
  # cat() the HTML: print() on a kableExtra table sends it to the viewer, not
  # into the document, when called from a results='asis' chunk
  cat(as.character(
    pepchem_glossary(ph = glossary_ph) |>
      kable(format = "html", caption = "Physicochemical descriptors") |>
      kable_paper("hover", full_width = FALSE) |>
      kableExtra::column_spec(1, bold = TRUE)
  ), "\n\n")
}
```
